battlecards.why_selected: Met 3.4% collection-based fee target, delivered >22% savings with no platform switch and limited disruption.
battlecards.contract_terms: 3-year term; fee = 3.4% of net collections; Year-3 price cap CPI+2%; Savida now covers credit-card processing fees; opportunity to renegotiate extension in Year-2.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Four credible bidders in RFP and benchmark data showing athena above market rates.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Deep integration with Savida workflows; proven MAT functionality; dedicated customer-success team.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Attempted price increase; CPI escalator risk; credit-card fees shifted to client.
battlecards.switching_costs: High—data migration, provider training, revenue-cycle downtime.
key_contacts: Molly Hebert – Group Sales Executive Manager
battlecards.notes: Re-engage athena in Year-2 to trade extension for elimination of CPI uplift.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Higher total cost after implementation fees and data-migration risk; athena matched target pricing.
battlecards.contract_terms: Proposed multi-year SaaS license for Aura platform with optional bundled RCM; pricing in 12/20/24 and 2/20/25 proposals.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Served mainly to pressure athena on pricing.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Behavioral-health focus, strong customization, positive peer references.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Migration complexity, unclear billing integration, higher upfront cost.
battlecards.switching_costs: Full data migration, training, workflow rebuild.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Did not meet Savida’s required pricing target; concerns about scalability for rapid-growth footprint.
battlecards.contract_terms: CareLogic SaaS proposal dated 12/6/2024; pricing valid through 3/6/2025.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Offered benchmark for market rates on behavioral-health EMRs.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Strong clinical documentation and reporting features.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Limited revenue-cycle track record; higher cost than athena after final round.
battlecards.switching_costs: High implementation fees plus staff retraining.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Workflow and disaster-recovery strengths noted but pricing and change-management effort outweighed benefits.
battlecards.contract_terms: Proposed PM + Billing platform with optional EI suite; detailed in RFP folder 12/02/24.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Helped establish ceiling on athena’s pricing.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Robust analytics, detailed DR plan, scalable cloud option.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Less proven in MAT specialty; implementation complexity.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Quoted 4%–4.5% of collections—above athena’s final offer; less referenceable in behavioral-health space.
battlecards.contract_terms: RCM + EMR proposal dated 1/07/25; sliding fee scale with volume.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Added competitive tension in final round.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Higher ongoing cost, limited behavioral-health references.

battlecards.why_selected: Access to aggregated GPO pricing on core SKUs with minimal operational change.
battlecards.contract_terms: Participating member agreement; pricing tied to Provista contracts; renews annually.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Large Provista member volume and benchmark comparisons.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Broad SKU coverage, automated rebates, no direct contract negotiation.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Compliance requirements to stay on-contract; limited brand flexibility.
battlecards.switching_costs: Low—roster upload and new ordering portal.
battlecards.notes: Savings validation of high-usage SKUs still underway.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Pricing above Provista contract rates on high-volume items.
battlecards.switching_costs: Low—users already familiar with online ordering interfaces.

battlecards.why_selected: Secured double-digit savings across lab and medical consumables with contract pricing and rebate opportunities.
battlecards.contract_terms: Member participation agreement signed 5/5/2025; pricing tied to Provista/Premier tiers; annual review.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Aggregated volume across Savida locations and Premier contract tiers.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Wide contract portfolio, electronic ordering, freight incentives.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Requires adherence to contract formulary; possible back-order risk on niche items.
battlecards.switching_costs: Location roster upload and item cross-reference; moderate.
battlecards.notes: Need to finalize temp-strip cup pricing to lock in savings.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Did not match Provista contract pricing on solvents and reagents.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Threat of moving volume to GPO contracts.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Higher pricing on high-volume SKUs; limited breadth for medical consumables.
battlecards.switching_costs: Moderate—new item numbers needed but no system integration.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Prices on gloves, caps, and deep-well plates exceeded Provista rates.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Ability to consolidate SKUs under Provista contract.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Responsive customer service; niche lab plastics.

battlecards.why_selected: Provided best like-for-like pricing and agreed to benchmark future purchases.
battlecards.contract_terms: Quote-based purchasing with option to piggyback on Provista IT contract pricing.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Benchmarked Dell and HP models across three VARs; used lowest quote to negotiate.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Aggressive pricing, multiple OEM lines, quick quote turnaround.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Requires case-by-case quoting; no existing e-procurement link.
battlecards.notes: Use Connection quotes to pressure CDW on future buys.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Could not match Connection’s quoted pricing on Dell OptiPlex and Latitude models.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Ability to shift upcoming laptop refresh to lower-priced VAR.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Existing account setup; Dell Premier access.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Higher unit pricing; limited pricing transparency.

battlecards.why_selected: Consolidation under single hierarchy reduced duplicate fees and enabled managed monitoring without changing last-mile provider.
battlecards.contract_terms: Pending agreement—standard 36-month term with TPX overlay; SLA for uptime & bandwidth.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Ability to consolidate 30+ location accounts and optimize bandwidth tiers.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Ubiquitous cable footprint; quick install intervals; TPX adds 24/7 monitoring.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Limited fiber availability in rural sites; past billing complexity.
battlecards.switching_costs: Medium—circuit re-provisioning and potential ETF if moved away.
battlecards.notes: Validate savings once final circuits and managed-service fee schedule are confirmed.
